scope.instance: One HttpClient or HttpServer resource ledger shared across its protocol pools and routes.
scope.owner: Canonical origin plus direct/proxy route identity; server connections share the listener owner.
scope.snapshot: One lock-consistent sample at sampledAt; current live counts are distinct from pre-connect and pre-stream reservations. High-water values represent peak admitted slots since instance creation.
scope.managedBuffers: Logical bytes held by admitted HTTP/2 received DATA segments and serialized write frames. This is not process RSS. HTTP parser limits, multipart scratch buffers, resolver caches/queues, per-pool wait queues, and synchronous observation callbacks keep their own stated bounds.

assertions: instance, route, and origin connection limits reject excess admission
connection factory reservations are reported separately from usable physical connections
close and failed factory creation release exactly one slot
one request attempt remains charged through its response body lifetime
request and origin ceilings are shared across HTTP/1 and HTTP/2
error, body close, and cancellation release after underlying work exits
stream reservations do not appear as active before an open stream exists
ordinary and promised streams share instance, route, and origin ceilings
reset, GOAWAY, connection close, and successful completion release once
received DATA is admitted before payload allocation and bounded by receive-window capacity
per-route and per-origin DATA bytes share the instance budget
control and cleanup capacity remains available when DATA capacity is saturated
partial read, discard, failure, and writer termination release the exact retained bytes
waiters never exceed the configured limit
cancellation and deadline remove waiter ownership promptly
a grant racing cancellation has one owner and one release
one busy owner cannot starve an eligible waiter from another owner
all fields correspond to one ledger lock interval
owner rows are unordered and keyed by origin plus route
logical managed bytes exclude runtime, native TLS, kernel, and caller-owned memory
snapshot capture time is monotonic and high-water values do not decrease
each independent limit states units, scope, default, and refusal/error behavior
DNS and pool queues remain separately bounded
observation hooks use no library queue
profiles record exact process limits and exit status
deterministic cap tests remain distinct from host-resource pressure
no OOM or killed process is counted as a normal refusal
